results.title: GPU rental prices are rising in 2026 — the dated evidence | GPUJournal
highlights:
### The verdict

- Nebius — Raised rates across the board. H100 SXM now $4.50/hr.
- RunPod Secure — Raised Secure Cloud rates. H200 $4.59 → $5.29/hr (▲ 15%); RTX 4090 $0.74 → $0.89/hr (▲ 20%).
- Verda — Three rises in four days — all nine rose on Oct 23 and Oct 26; seven of nine rose again on Oct 24. H100 SXM $4.34 → $4.61/hr (▲ 6.2%).
- The cheapest offers — No movement in our records. The best verified H100 offer is still $2.25/hr.

## The evidence, date by date

Every rise below was read on the provider's own published pricing page on both sides of the change — the before figure and the after figure, each with its date. That is the standard our Price Watch applies to every entry. October 1 — Nebius raises across the board: Nebius lifted its on-demand rates at the start of October, and our board carries the post-rise rates (H100 $4.50/hr, H200 $5.40/hr, B200 $8.50/hr, verified Oct 19 and re-read unchanged Oct 26). October 14 — RunPod Secure goes up: RTX 4090 rose from $0.74 to $0.89/hr (▲ 20%) and H200 from $4.59 to $5.29/hr (▲ 15%) on RunPod's Secure Cloud; both rates were re-read on RunPod's own page on Oct 24 and Oct 26 — unchanged since the rise. October 23, 24 and 26 — Verda rises three times in four days: all nine Verda GPUs rose on Oct 23 and again on Oct 26, and seven of the nine rose on Oct 24 as well (A100 40GB and L40S held that day) — the full table is below. We are not the only ones seeing it: a third-party analysis published Oct 21, 2026 found H100 prices up at six of seven specialist GPU clouds during 2026. Our own records cover October in daily detail; the direction agrees.

### Verda — three rises in four days, in full

All figures USD per GPU per hour, read on verda.com/pricing on each date shown.

| GPU | Oct 22 | Oct 23 | Oct 24 | Oct 26 | 4-day move |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $4.34 | $4.51 | $4.56 | $4.61 | ▲ 6.2% |
| H200 | $5.66 | $5.89 | $5.95 | $6.01 | ▲ 6.2% |
| B200 | $8.07 | $8.36 | $8.44 | $8.52 | ▲ 5.6% |
| B300 | $10.28 | $10.69 | $10.80 | $10.91 | ▲ 6.1% |
| GB300 | $11.82 | $12.29 | $12.42 | $12.55 | ▲ 6.2% |
| A100 80GB | $2.07 | $2.13 | $2.15 | $2.16 | ▲ 4.3% |
| A100 40GB | $1.52 | $1.56 | $1.56 | $1.58 | ▲ 3.9% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | $2.40 | $2.49 | $2.52 | $2.54 | ▲ 5.8% |
| L40S | $1.77 | $1.81 | $1.81 | $1.83 | ▲ 3.4% |

### The half that has not moved

Against those rises, the cheapest verified offers on our board did not move at all during the week of Oct 19–26:

| GPU | Best verified offer | Provider | Oct 19 → Oct 26 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $2.25/hr | TensorDock (8-GPU minimum) | — unchanged |
| H200 | $3.59/hr | RunPod Community | — unchanged |
| B200 | $5.98/hr | RunPod Community | — unchanged |
| RTX 4090 | $0.20/hr | nafnaf | — unchanged |
| A100 80GB | $1.09/hr | Thunder Compute | — unchanged |

Read the terms before you chase the floor — minimum commitments and community-cloud availability differ from list-rate clouds. But the fact stands: on Oct 26 you could still rent an H100 for roughly half the rate a rising list price asks ($2.25 vs $4.50–$4.61). Rising list prices have not pulled the floor up — yet.

...

### How we know

GPUJournal reads providers' own published pricing pages and banks the figures at every check. The checks behind this page fell on Oct 19, 22, 23, 24 and 26, 2026 — there are gaps between them, so the October rises are documented check by check rather than day by day. A price change we catch in our own checks is only reported when both the before and after figures were seen on the provider's own page, each with its date; that is how the Verda and RunPod rises above were verified. The Nebius rise of Oct 1, 2026 is different: it predates our records and was an announced rise, so we did not bank both sides of it ourselves — we verified the post-rise rates on Nebius's own page (checked Oct 19, re-read unchanged Oct 26) and report it as announced. And a price a provider merely states about itself never appears on our board as a verified price. Where a provider's pages state figures we cannot verify, Price Watch reports them labelled as stated — which is how disagreements get exposed rather than hidden: on Oct 26, Spheron's pages stated the same H100 at $2.64 on some pages and $2.98 on others, and we report the disagreement rather than pick a number.

results.title: Four pricing changes in eight days at one provider. None at another. | Compute Stacker
results.author: Compute Stacker
highlights:
# Four pricing changes in eight days at one provider. None at another. | Compute Stacker · LinkedIn · 2026-10-27T00:00:00+00:00

**Compute Stacker**.

---

Four pricing changes in eight days at one provider. None at another.

What actually happened on H100 rate cards this month:

- October 1: Nebius raised on-demand H100 from $3.85 to $4.50, up 16.9%, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50, up 21%. Its second increase in three months.
- October 7: AWS reserved Capacity Blocks moved to $5.970 per H100 accelerator-hour, the same rate across twelve regions.
- October 8: Nebius switched preemptible H100, H200, B200, B300 and RTX PRO 6000 to dynamic spot pricing. The published $2.15 became a floor of $0.79, with prices that can change every 15 minutes, including during a run, capped one cent below the on-demand rate.
- CoreWeave's HGX H100 node stayed at $49.24, or $6.16 per GPU.

Five things a headline rate doesn't tell you:

1. Per GPU or per node. CoreWeave, Oracle, Google and Azure sell H100s as 8-GPU nodes. If you need three, you pay for eight.
2. Volume rules. AWS charges $5.970 whether you take one GPU or eight. Lambda charges $4.29 for one and $3.99 each for eight.
3. Region. Nebius's H100 is in eu-north1 only. Google's 8-GPU H100 varies about 30% between its cheapest and priciest regions.
4. Purchase type. On-demand, spot, reserved and committed can differ by more than 3x on the same chip, with completely different reliability.
5. What's bundled. Lambda and CoreWeave list free egress. AWS charges about $0.09 per GB after an allowance.

results.title: GPU Rental Price Report, November 2026 · EverXCloud
highlights:
# GPU Rental Price Report, November 2026

Public GPU-hour prices for H100, H200, B200, A100, L40S, RTX 4090 and RTX 5090 across 16 cloud providers, with medians and spreads.

## Executive summary

EverXCloud read the public pricing pages of 16 GPU cloud providers on 2026-10-26 and recorded 75 prices per GPU-hour for eight GPUs. On-demand prices for the same GPU still vary widely between providers, and spot, preemptible or community capacity costs far less than on-demand capacity.

This report covers third-party list prices only. Once the EverXCloud Marketplace launches, its own price index will be published from real transactions.

## Key findings

1. The median on-demand H100 SXM price across 11 providers is $3.99 per GPU-hour, from $3.14 to $6.16: the most expensive listing costs 2.0× the cheapest.
2. Spot, preemptible and community H100 SXM capacity has a median of $2.30 per GPU-hour across 3 providers, 42% below the on-demand median.
3. The H200 carries a 24% premium over the H100 SXM at the median ($4.94 vs $3.99 on demand, 10 providers).
4. On-demand B200 prices range from $6.00 to $8.60 per GPU-hour across 7 providers, with a median of $8.19.
5. The A100 80GB shows the widest relative spread among data center GPUs: 2.6× between the cheapest ($1.09) and the most expensive ($2.79) on-demand listing, across 9 providers.
6. AWS Capacity Blocks, a short-term reservation, list the H100 at $5.97 and the B200 at $14.21 per GPU-hour, 1.5× and 1.7× the on-demand medians of the other providers.

## Prices by GPU

On-demand, USD per GPU-hour

| GPU | Min | Median | Max | Max ÷ min | Providers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $3.14 | $3.99 | $6.16 | 2.0× | 11 |
| H100 PCIe | $2.89 | $3.29 | $3.50 | 1.2× | 3 |
| H200 | $3.62 | $4.94 | $6.30 | 1.7× | 10 |
| B200 | $6.00 | $8.19 | $8.60 | 1.4× | 7 |
| A100 80GB | $1.09 | $1.49 | $2.79 | 2.6× | 9 |
| L40S | $0.97 | $1.56 | $2.25 | 2.3× | 6 |
| RTX 4090 | $0.39 | $0.64 | $0.89 | 2.3× | 3 |
| RTX 5090 | $0.65 | $0.92 | $1.19 | 1.8× | 2 |

...

- Prices were read on 2026-10-26 on each provider's official public pricing page, in USD per GPU-hour, excluding tax. No price was estimated, negotiated or taken from a third-party aggregator.
- One price per provider, GPU and offer type. When a provider lists several configurations for the same GPU, the lowest listed price was kept, and the listing is recorded in the data.
- Multi-GPU instances are converted to a per-GPU price by dividing the instance price by the number of GPUs (for example CoreWeave and AWS 8-GPU instances).
- On-demand and spot, preemptible or community prices are reported separately. AWS prices are Capacity Block rates, a short-term reservation, and are not included in the on-demand statistics.
- Providers whose pricing page could not be read, showed prices only after sign-in or on request, or did not map prices to GPUs unambiguously were left out: Vast.ai, Crusoe, Vultr, TensorDock, Fluidstack, Genesis Cloud, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Voltage Park, Cudo Compute, Scaleway, Paperspace and SF Compute.
- The median of an even number of prices is the mean of the two middle values.

highlights:
What an NVIDIA H100 costs to rent (Nov 2026): from $1.99/hr

# What it costs to rent an NVIDIA H100

NVIDIA H100 prices from every provider listed here, what changes them, and what a month costs.

Prices as of 14 Nov 2026, 14:19 UTC

An NVIDIA H100 rents from $1.99 per GPU-hour on-demand and $1.29 on spot, across the 6 providers listed here. The tables below are this site's current prices: they change when the providers' prices do.

## Every provider's cheapest H100 price

Per GPU per hour, for each version and pricing type. A month is 730 hours of continuous use.

| Provider | Version | Pricing | Per GPU-hour | For 730 hours |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Azure | NVL 94 GB | Spot | $1.29 | $942 |
| RunPod | PCIe 80 GB | On-demand | $1.99 | $1,453 |
| Azure | SXM 80 GB | Spot | $2.27 | $1,658 |
| Vultr | 80 GB, version not stated | Spot | $2.30 | $1,679 |
| Nebius | SXM 80 GB | Spot | $2.37 | $1,730 |
| RunPod | NVL 94 GB | On-demand | $2.59 | $1,891 |
| RunPod | SXM 80 GB | On-demand | $2.69 | $1,964 |
| Scaleway | PCIe 80 GB | On-demand | $3.17 | $2,313 |
| Scaleway | SXM 80 GB | On-demand | $3.50 | $2,555 |
| Scaleway | version not stated | On-demand | $5.30 | $3,868 |
| AWS | SXM 80 GB | On-demand | $6.88 | $5,022 |
| Azure | NVL 94 GB | On-demand | $6.98 | $5,095 |
| Azure | SXM 80 GB | On-demand | $12.29 | $8,972 |

...

## What changes the price

The version. On-demand, the PCIe 80 GB starts at $1.99, the NVL 94 GB starts at $2.59 and the SXM 80 GB starts at $2.69. PCIe is a card that fits a standard server slot. It runs at lower power than SXM and links to other GPUs more slowly, and it is usually the cheaper version to rent. NVL is a PCIe card made to be paired with a second one over an NVLink bridge, so the two share data quickly. It draws less power than the SXM version. SXM is a module mounted on NVIDIA's HGX board, where GPUs share data over NVLink. It runs at full power with the fastest links between GPUs, which is why 8-GPU training machines use it.

The pricing type. The cheapest spot price, $1.29 at Azure, is 35% below the cheapest on-demand price. Spot capacity can be taken back at short notice; see spot or on-demand.

The provider. Each provider's cheapest on-demand price runs from $1.99 at RunPod to $6.98 at Azure: 3.5 times as much for the same GPU family.

The region. Azure charges $12.29 per GPU-hour for its Standard_ND96isr_H100_v5 in US West 3 and $21.64 in ZA North, for the same machine.

## A month of H100 time

One H100 for a month of 730 hours costs $1,453 at the cheapest on-demand price. On spot it is $942, if the capacity is not taken back. Eight of them for the same month come to $11,622 at that rate; the cheapest whole eight-GPU machine listed here, p5.48xlarge at AWS, is $40,179.

...

Prices are each provider's list price in US dollars per GPU per hour, excluding tax, as of the time shown. Spot capacity can be interrupted and is shown apart from on-demand. Nothing here is a quote or an offer; check the provider before you rent. Euro prices are converted at the European Central Bank rate for 13 Nov 2026.

Why one cloud quotes a GPU and another a whole machine, and how this site puts them on one scale.

# Spot or on-demand GPUs

What spot GPUs save against on-demand, GPU by GPU, and what you give up for it.

Prices as of 14 Nov 2026, 00:51 UTC

Spot capacity is spare capacity a cloud rents for less, on the condition that it can take it back at short notice. Across the 14 GPUs listed here with both prices, spot runs from 14% to 82% below on-demand.
